title: load_sidecar_positions returns raw, un-normalised coordinates; submodel route injects NaN/Inf/non-numeric positions unvalidated (asymmetry vs parse_pipeline_to_graph)
description: The main graph path normalises sidecar positions through `_normalise_sidecar_positions` (parse_pipeline_to_graph line 731), which rejects non-dict entries, booleans-as-numbers, non-numeric x/y, and crucially non-finite values via `math.isfinite` (lines 790-797). The submodel path does NOT: `load_sidecar_positions` (637-640) returns `dict(load_sidecar(py_path).get('positions', {}))` verbatim, and its sole caller routes/submodel.py:120-124 applies them via `node.model_copy(update={'position': positions[node.id]})`. GraphNode has no `validate_assignment` config (only PipelineGraph carries a model_config, and it is just `ignored_types`), and Pydantic v2 `model_copy(update=...)` performs a raw __dict__ update with NO validation. Therefore a hand-crafted submodel `.haute.json` containing e.g. `{"positions": {"n1": {"x": NaN, "y": 0}}}` (json.loads parses NaN by default) or `{"x": "abc", "y": 1}` flows straight into node.position. When the SubmodelGraphResponse is serialised back to the client this yields invalid JSON (`NaN`/`Infinity` tokens that break strict frontend parsers) for non-finite coords, or a 500 from response-model validation for a non-numeric coord. The main pipeline GET is immune to the identical corrupt input because it funnels through `_normalise_sidecar_positions`; the submodel GET is not. This is a real robustness/contract asymmetry whose root cause is that `load_sidecar_positions` does not reuse the normalisation helper that already exists in this same module. Fix: have `load_sidecar_positions` return `_normalise_sidecar_positions(load_sidecar(py_path).get('positions'))` (or have the submodel caller normalise), so both code paths share one position-hygiene contract.
evidence: load_sidecar_positions: `result = load_sidecar(py_path).get('positions', {}); return dict(result) if isinstance(result, dict) else {}` — no per-coordinate validation. parse_pipeline_to_graph instead calls `_normalise_sidecar_positions(sidecar.get('positions'))` (731) which drops non-finite via `if not math.isfinite(xf) or not math.isfinite(yf): continue` (796-797). Caller submodel.py:124 `node.model_copy(update={'position': positions[node.id]})`; GraphNode (_types.py:602-608) has no model_config → no validate_assignment; Pydantic v2 model_copy(update) skips validation. Tests TestLoadSidecarPositions (test_route_helpers.py:264-281) only cover valid + missing-key cases, never malformed coordinates, so the gap is uncovered.
behavior_preservation: Routing through _normalise_sidecar_positions leaves all well-formed positions unchanged (the existing valid-case tests still pass) and only drops/ignores malformed or non-finite coordinates, matching the main pipeline path.
